Title: Baseball Trivia
Description: 118 questions covering MLB history, rules, records, legendary players, iconic World Series moments, ballparks, and baseball culture.

Questions.Prompt: How many players from each team are on the field defensively during a standard baseball inning?
Questions.Explanation: A defensive team fields nine players: pitcher, catcher, four infielders, and three outfielders.

Questions.Prompt: How many balls does a batter need to be awarded before taking first base on a walk?
Questions.Explanation: Four pitches called balls result in a base on balls, sending the batter to first.

Questions.Prompt: How many strikes result in a batter being called out?
Questions.Explanation: Three strikes and the batter is out, whether the strikes are swinging, called, or foul (with limits on foul bunts).

Questions.Prompt: What is it called when a batter hits a fly ball out of the park in fair territory, scoring at least one run?
Questions.Explanation: A home run allows the batter (and any runners on base) to round all bases and score.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes a home run hit with the bases loaded, scoring four runs at once?
Questions.Explanation: A grand slam is the maximum possible runs on a single home run - one for each runner plus the batter.

Questions.Prompt: What is it called when a player hits a single, double, triple, and home run all in the same game?
Questions.Explanation: Hitting for the cycle is a rare offensive feat requiring all four types of hits in one game.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a play where the batting team's runner scores the winning run in the bottom of the final inning, immediately ending the game?
Questions.Explanation: A walk-off ends the game instantly because the home team, batting last, has already won - no more outs are needed.

Questions.Prompt: What is a 'balk' in baseball?
Options: An illegal motion by the pitcher with runners on base, awarding them the next base
A batter stepping out of the box mid-pitch
A foul ball caught for an out
Questions.Explanation: A balk penalizes a pitcher for a deceptive or illegal motion meant to unfairly hold or trick baserunners.

Questions.Prompt: What is the 'infield fly rule' designed to prevent?
Options: Infielders intentionally dropping an easy pop fly to turn a cheap double play
Pitchers throwing too many pickoff attempts
Questions.Explanation: With runners on first and second (or bases loaded) and fewer than two outs, an infield fly is automatically ruled out to stop a cheap double-play trick.

Questions.Prompt: What is a 'sacrifice fly'?
Options: A fly ball caught for an out that allows a runner to tag up and score
A bunt that advances a runner
A fly ball that lands foul
Questions.Explanation: A sacrifice fly doesn't count as an official at-bat against the batter's average, even though it's an out, because it drove in a run.

Questions.Prompt: What defensive statistic credits a pitcher with ending a game while protecting a lead under specific conditions?
Questions.Explanation: A save is awarded to a relief pitcher who finishes a close game his team wins without giving up the lead.

Questions.Prompt: What batting statistic combines on-base percentage and slugging percentage into a single number widely used in modern analysis?
Options: WHIP (Walks and Hits per Inning Pitched)
Questions.Explanation: OPS adds a hitter's on-base percentage to their slugging percentage as a quick overall offensive measure.

Questions.Prompt: What pitching statistic measures the average number of baserunners (via walks and hits) allowed per inning?
Questions.Explanation: WHIP (Walks plus Hits per Inning Pitched) shows how many baserunners a pitcher typically allows each inning.

Questions.Prompt: What sabermetric statistic attempts to estimate how many more wins a player is worth compared to a readily available replacement-level player?
Questions.Explanation: WAR compresses a player's total offensive, defensive, and pitching value into one comprehensive number.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes a play where a defensive team records three outs on a single continuous play?
Questions.Explanation: Triple plays are among the rarest defensive feats in baseball, often occurring on a sharp line drive with runners moving.

Questions.Prompt: What is an 'unassisted triple play,' one of the rarest plays in baseball?
Options: A single fielder recording all three outs of a triple play alone
A triple play completed without any errors
Three consecutive strikeouts by one pitcher
A triple play ending an inning and a game simultaneously
Questions.Explanation: An unassisted triple play typically happens when a middle infielder catches a liner, steps on second, and tags a runner - all without help.

Questions.Prompt: What is a 'ground-rule double'?
Options: A fair ball that bounces over the outfield fence or gets stuck in a defined obstruction, automatically awarding the batter second base
A double hit directly down the foul line
A double where the batter is thrown out trying for third
A ball that hits the foul pole
Questions.Explanation: Ground-rule doubles are governed by each park's specific field rules for balls that leave play in unusual ways.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes a batter leading their league in batting average, home runs, and RBIs in the same season?
Questions.Explanation: Winning the Triple Crown is one of the rarest offensive achievements; Miguel Cabrera won the last MLB Triple Crown in 2012.

Questions.Prompt: What milestone is reached by a pitcher who records 300 career wins, a benchmark achieved by only a handful of pitchers in modern history?
Questions.Explanation: Randy Johnson was the most recent pitcher to reach 300 career wins, in 2009 - a feat increasingly rare in the modern bullpen era.

Questions.Prompt: What exclusive career hitting milestone has been reached by legends like Pete Rose, Ty Cobb, and Derek Jeter?
Questions.Explanation: Membership in the 3,000-hit club is one of the surest tickets to the Hall of Fame in baseball history.

Questions.Prompt: Who holds the all-time MLB record for career stolen bases, nicknamed 'The Man of Steal'?
Questions.Explanation: Rickey Henderson stole 1,406 career bases, a record widely considered unbreakable in the modern game.

Questions.Prompt: Who holds the MLB all-time career saves record among relief pitchers?
Questions.Explanation: Mariano Rivera finished his career with 652 saves, largely built on his legendary cut fastball for the Yankees.

Questions.Prompt: What award is given annually to the best pitcher in each league, named after a legendary early-1900s hurler?
Questions.Explanation: Cy Young won 511 career games, and MLB has honored the sport's top pitchers with his namesake award since 1956.

Questions.Prompt: How many career National League and American League MVP awards did Barry Bonds win, the most of any player in history?
Questions.Explanation: Barry Bonds won a record seven MVP awards, including four consecutive from 2001 to 2004.

Questions.Prompt: What underdog 1969 team, previously a perennial last-place club, stunned baseball by winning the World Series?
Questions.Explanation: The 1969 'Miracle Mets' went from lovable losers to World Series champions in just their eighth season of existence.

Questions.Prompt: What error by first baseman Bill Buckner in Game 6 of the 1986 World Series became one of the most infamous plays in baseball history?
Options: A ground ball rolled through his legs, allowing the winning run to score
He dropped a routine pop fly
He threw the ball into the stands
He missed the base on a force out
Questions.Explanation: Mookie Wilson's slow roller got past Buckner, letting the Mets complete a comeback and eventually win the Series against the Red Sox.

Questions.Prompt: Whose dramatic pinch-hit walk-off home run, despite two bad knees, won Game 1 of the 1988 World Series for the Dodgers?
Questions.Explanation: Kirk Gibson could barely walk but limped around the bases after his iconic home run off Dennis Eckersley.

Questions.Prompt: What Boston catcher famously waved his fly ball fair with his arms in Game 6 of the 1975 World Series before it hit the foul pole for a home run?
Questions.Explanation: Carlton Fisk's body-language 'wave it fair' gesture became one of the most replayed moments in World Series history.

Questions.Prompt: Which slugger earned the nickname 'Mr. October' after hitting three home runs on three consecutive pitches in Game 6 of the 1977 World Series?
Questions.Explanation: Reggie Jackson's three-homer game for the Yankees against the Dodgers cemented his clutch postseason legacy.

Questions.Prompt: What injury did Curt Schilling famously pitch through during the 2004 postseason, visible as blood soaking through his sock?
Options: A torn tendon sheath in his ankle
Questions.Explanation: Schilling's 'Bloody Sock' start became legendary as the Red Sox completed their historic comeback against the Yankees en route to the title.

Questions.Prompt: What is the record for most games played in a single World Series before the format was standardized to a best-of-seven?
Options: Eight games (best-of-nine format, used in 1903 and 1919-1921)
Questions.Explanation: MLB briefly experimented with a best-of-nine World Series format in the early 1900s before settling on best-of-seven.

Questions.Prompt: What was the first MLB team to win a World Series after entering the playoffs as a Wild Card, doing so in 2002?
Questions.Explanation: The Anaheim Angels became the first Wild Card team to win it all, defeating the San Francisco Giants in seven games.

Questions.Prompt: What over-the-shoulder, back-to-home-plate catch by Willie Mays in the 1954 World Series is simply known as 'The Catch'?
Options: A running grab of a deep fly ball at the Polo Grounds
A diving catch at the warning track
A leaping catch over the outfield wall
A bare-handed catch at first base
Questions.Explanation: Willie Mays' basket catch running away from home plate is considered one of the greatest defensive plays ever filmed.

Questions.Prompt: What poignant phrase did Lou Gehrig use to describe himself in his 1939 farewell speech at Yankee Stadium after his ALS diagnosis?
Options: 'The luckiest man on the face of the earth'
Questions.Explanation: Gehrig's Farewell Speech, delivered as his career ended tragically early due to illness, remains one of sports' most emotional moments.

Questions.Prompt: What was the highest single-season batting average recorded in the modern era, set by Ted Williams in 1941 and never matched since?
Questions.Explanation: Ted Williams hit .406 in 1941 - no MLB player has batted .400 or better in a full season since.

Questions.Prompt: Which Hall of Fame pitcher famously chose not to pitch Game 1 of the 1965 World Series because it fell on Yom Kippur?
Questions.Explanation: Sandy Koufax's decision to observe the Jewish holy day rather than pitch became a landmark moment beyond baseball.

Questions.Prompt: Who became the second player in MLB history to reach 3,000 hits while also becoming a symbol of humanitarian service, dying in a 1972 plane crash delivering aid?
Questions.Explanation: Roberto Clemente reached exactly 3,000 hits in his final regular-season at-bat before his tragic death delivering earthquake relief supplies.

Questions.Prompt: Who holds the MLB record for most career hits, despite being permanently banned from baseball for gambling on games?
Questions.Explanation: Pete Rose's 4,256 career hits remain the all-time record, though his gambling ban has kept him out of the Hall of Fame.

Questions.Prompt: What single-season MLB hits record, set in 2004, is held by Ichiro Suzuki?
Questions.Explanation: Ichiro Suzuki's 262 hits in 2004 broke George Sisler's 84-year-old single-season record.

Questions.Prompt: What Yankees shortstop, nicknamed 'The Captain,' retired in 2014 with over 3,400 career hits, all with one franchise?
Questions.Explanation: Derek Jeter spent his entire 20-year Hall of Fame career with the New York Yankees, winning five World Series titles.

Questions.Prompt: What is the name of the annual award given to the best rookie in each league, honoring the man who broke baseball's color barrier?
Options: The Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year Award
The Comeback Player of the Year Award
Questions.Explanation: MLB officially renamed the Rookie of the Year Award after Jackie Robinson in 1987, forty years after his historic debut.

Questions.Prompt: What Chicago ballpark, home of the Cubs, is famous for its ivy-covered outfield walls and didn't install lights for night games until 1988?
Questions.Explanation: Wrigley Field, opened in 1914, was the last MLB ballpark to add lights, hosting its first official night game on August 8, 1988.

Questions.Prompt: What nickname is given to the original Yankee Stadium, built in 1923 to house the growing legend of Babe Ruth?
Questions.Explanation: Yankee Stadium earned its nickname because Ruth's popularity directly funded its construction.

Questions.Prompt: What Baltimore ballpark, opened in 1992, is widely credited with sparking the modern trend of retro, downtown-style baseball stadiums?
Questions.Explanation: Camden Yards blended old-fashioned brick architecture with modern amenities, inspiring nearly every ballpark built since.

Questions.Prompt: What Colorado ballpark's high altitude is famous for causing baseballs to travel farther, contributing to unusually high-scoring games?
Questions.Explanation: Coors Field sits roughly a mile above sea level in Denver, where thinner air famously helps fly balls carry further.

Questions.Prompt: What is the name of the domed, permanently roofed stadium home to the Tampa Bay Rays?
Questions.Explanation: Tropicana Field's cable-supported dome and famously quirky catwalks have made it one of MLB's most distinctive ballparks.

Questions.Prompt: What material are official MLB bats required to be made of, unlike aluminum bats commonly used in amateur baseball?
Questions.Explanation: MLB requires solid wood bats, typically ash, maple, or birch, unlike the metal bats used at lower levels of the sport.

Questions.Prompt: What informal nickname do catchers give their bulky protective gear (mask, chest protector, shin guards)?
Questions.Explanation: The self-deprecating nickname pokes fun at how tough (or foolish) you'd have to be to willingly crouch behind home plate all game.

Questions.Prompt: What controversial 1983 incident involved Kansas City's George Brett having a home run controversially disallowed for excess pine tar on his bat?
Questions.Explanation: Brett's furious dugout charge after umpires nullified his go-ahead homer became one of baseball's most memorable meltdowns - later overturned by the league.

Questions.Prompt: What pitch, once common but banned by MLB in 1920 due to safety and fairness concerns, involved doctoring the ball with saliva or other substances?
Questions.Explanation: The spitball was outlawed largely for safety reasons after a batter was killed by a doctored pitch he couldn't see clearly.

Questions.Prompt: In what year did the American League first adopt the designated hitter (DH) rule, allowing a substitute for the pitcher's spot in the batting order?
Questions.Explanation: The AL introduced the DH in 1973 as an experiment to boost offense; the National League didn't adopt it full-time until 2022.

Questions.Prompt: What position is responsible for calling pitches, blocking wild pitches, and defending home plate?
Questions.Explanation: The catcher squats behind home plate, working closely with the pitcher to call and receive every pitch of the game.

Questions.Prompt: How many total bases are there on a standard baseball diamond, including home plate?
Questions.Explanation: A diamond has first, second, third base, and home plate, forming the four corners a runner must touch to score.

Questions.Prompt: What is the standard distance between each base on a Major League Baseball diamond?
Questions.Explanation: The 90-foot base paths have remained unchanged since the 19th century, a distance considered nearly perfectly balanced between offense and defense.

Questions.Prompt: What longtime New York Yankees and Mets manager was famous for his colorful, rambling quotes known as 'Stengelese'?
Questions.Explanation: Casey Stengel managed the Yankees to seven World Series titles in the 1950s while entertaining reporters with his unique verbal style.

Questions.Prompt: Who holds the record for most seasons managing a single MLB franchise, leading the Philadelphia Athletics for 50 years?
Questions.Explanation: Connie Mack managed (and largely owned) the Athletics from 1901 to 1950, an unmatched tenure in professional sports history.

Questions.Prompt: What Brooklyn Dodgers general manager is credited with signing Jackie Robinson and breaking baseball's color barrier?
Questions.Explanation: Branch Rickey scouted and signed Robinson specifically to integrate the major leagues, a decision that reshaped the sport forever.

Questions.Prompt: What fiery Yankees manager, known for his volatile relationship with owner George Steinbrenner, was hired and fired by the team five separate times?
Questions.Explanation: Billy Martin's tumultuous, on-again-off-again tenure managing the Yankees became a defining storyline of the franchise's late 1970s and 80s.

Questions.Prompt: What Japanese slugger holds the world professional baseball career home run record with 868, more than any MLB player?
Questions.Explanation: Sadaharu Oh hit 868 home runs playing for the Yomiuri Giants in Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball league.

Questions.Prompt: What international tournament, first held in 2006, features national teams from around the world competing in a baseball championship?
Questions.Explanation: The World Baseball Classic showcases MLB stars representing their home countries, distinct from the amateur Baseball World Cup.

Questions.Prompt: In 2020, MLB officially recognized the statistics and records of which historic set of leagues, elevating them to 'major league' status?
Questions.Explanation: MLB's 2020 decision recognized seven Negro Leagues (1920-1948) as major leagues, incorporating their statistics into official records.

Questions.Prompt: What legendary Negro Leagues pitcher, known for his showmanship and blazing fastball, later became the oldest rookie in MLB history at age 42?
Questions.Explanation: Satchel Paige finally reached the majors with the Cleveland Indians in 1948 after a legendary career in the Negro Leagues.

Questions.Prompt: Which country has produced more MLB players per capita than any other outside the United States, especially from towns like San Pedro de Macoris?
Questions.Explanation: The Dominican Republic has become one of baseball's richest talent pipelines, producing stars from Sammy Sosa to Pedro Martinez.

Questions.Prompt: What Pennsylvania town has hosted the Little League World Series every summer since 1947?
Questions.Explanation: Williamsport, Pennsylvania is the birthplace of Little League Baseball and remains the permanent host of its world series.

Questions.Prompt: What Nebraska city has hosted the NCAA College World Series for decades, first at Rosenblatt Stadium and now at Charles Schwab Field?
Questions.Explanation: Omaha has been synonymous with the College World Series since it began hosting the tournament in 1950.

Questions.Prompt: What traditional song is sung by fans during the seventh-inning stretch at nearly every MLB game?
Options: 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game'
Questions.Explanation: Written in 1908, 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game' has become baseball's unofficial anthem, sung during the stretch since the mid-1970s.

Questions.Prompt: What legendary broadcaster called Los Angeles Dodgers games for 67 seasons, famous for his warm, storytelling style?
Questions.Explanation: Vin Scully's tenure with the Dodgers, from Brooklyn to LA, ran from 1950 to 2016, making him one of broadcasting's most beloved voices.

Questions.Prompt: What 1989 film starring Kevin Costner featured the famous line 'If you build it, he will come' about a mysterious Iowa cornfield baseball diamond?
Questions.Explanation: Field of Dreams turned an Iowa farm into a real-life tourist destination, still hosting MLB games decades later.

Questions.Prompt: What 2011 film, based on a Michael Lewis book, dramatized the Oakland Athletics' use of sabermetrics to build a competitive roster on a tight budget?
Questions.Explanation: Moneyball starred Brad Pitt as GM Billy Beane, chronicling the A's data-driven approach that reshaped how front offices evaluate players.

Questions.Prompt: What technology, expanded across MLB starting in 2014, allows managers to challenge close calls for video review by umpires?
Questions.Explanation: Managers can challenge certain calls, triggering a video review by umpires in a centralized replay center to confirm or overturn the ruling.

Questions.Prompt: What rule, introduced across MLB in 2023 to speed up games, limits the time a pitcher has between pitches?
Questions.Explanation: The pitch clock forces pitchers to begin their motion within a set number of seconds, dramatically shortening average game times.

Questions.Prompt: In what year did the National League adopt the designated hitter rule on a permanent, universal basis?
Questions.Explanation: After decades of AL-only use, the NL adopted the universal DH starting with the 2022 season.

Questions.Prompt: What extra-innings rule, adopted by MLB starting in 2020, places a runner on second base to begin each half-inning past the ninth?
Questions.Explanation: Originally introduced to shorten games during the pandemic-shortened season, the runner-on-second rule became a permanent fixture for extra innings.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes a pitcher throwing at least one complete game without allowing any opposing batter to reach base by any means?
Questions.Explanation: A perfect game is even rarer than a no-hitter, requiring 27 consecutive batters retired with zero walks, hits, or errors.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a batter deliberately tapping the ball a short distance to advance a runner or reach base via a soft, controlled hit?
Questions.Explanation: Bunts are often used strategically as sacrifice plays to advance runners, or as a surprise attempt to reach base on a fast infield roller.

Questions.Prompt: What defensive strategy involves shifting infielders heavily to one side of the field based on a hitter's known tendencies?
Questions.Explanation: Defensive shifts became a major strategic trend in the 2010s before MLB limited them with new positioning rules in 2023.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a pitcher who enters the game specifically to face one batter, often a same-handed matchup, before being replaced?
Options: A LOOGY (Lefty One-Out GuY) / situational reliever
Questions.Explanation: LOOGY is baseball slang for a left-handed specialist brought in for a very short, matchup-specific appearance.

Questions.Prompt: What position is primarily responsible for covering the area between second and third base, often considered the most demanding defensive infield spot?
Questions.Explanation: Shortstop requires a strong arm, quick reflexes, and excellent range, making it one of the most valuable defensive positions.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes an out recorded when a fielder throws the ball to a base ahead of a runner attempting to advance, forcing them out without a tag?
Questions.Explanation: Force outs happen when a runner has no choice but to advance because a following batter-runner is occupying their previous base.

Questions.Prompt: What defensive statistic tracks the number of times a fielder successfully participates in recording an out without directly making the tag or catch?
Questions.Explanation: Assists are credited to fielders whose throw helps another player record an out, most commonly on a groundball to an infielder.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes an inning in which a pitcher retires all three batters without allowing a hit, walk, or error?
Questions.Explanation: A 1-2-3 inning is the most efficient possible outcome for a pitcher, facing the minimum three batters.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for the area behind home plate, first base, and third base where foul balls and pop-ups often occur?
Questions.Explanation: Foul territory varies significantly in size between ballparks, affecting how many foul pop-ups turn into outs.

Questions.Prompt: What is a 'pickle,' the informal term for a common baserunning situation?
Options: A rundown between two bases where a runner is trapped by fielders
A close play at home plate
Questions.Explanation: In a pickle (rundown), fielders throw the ball back and forth trying to tag out a runner caught between bases.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a batter who hits from both the left and right sides of the plate depending on the pitcher?
Questions.Explanation: Switch hitters gain a platoon advantage by always batting from the side opposite the pitcher's throwing hand.

Questions.Prompt: What midseason exhibition, first played in 1933, brings together the best players from the American and National Leagues each summer?
Questions.Explanation: The All-Star Game, nicknamed the 'Midsummer Classic,' has been a summer tradition since 1933, aside from a brief pandemic pause.

Questions.Prompt: What award, given annually since 1957, honors the best defensive player at each position in each league?
Questions.Explanation: The Gold Glove Award recognizes standout fielding performances, voted on by managers and coaches.

Questions.Prompt: What award, first given in 1980, recognizes the best offensive player at each defensive position in each league?
Questions.Explanation: The Silver Slugger Award complements the Gold Glove by honoring hitting excellence rather than fielding.

Questions.Prompt: What annual exhibition event, held the night before the All-Star Game, features sluggers competing to hit the most home runs?
Questions.Explanation: The Home Run Derby has become one of MLB's most popular standalone events, often drawing bigger TV audiences than the All-Star Game itself.

Questions.Prompt: What trophy is awarded annually to the winner of the World Series?
Questions.Explanation: The Commissioner's Trophy, featuring flags representing every MLB team, has been presented to World Series champions since 1967.

Questions.Prompt: What two leagues merged in 1903 to form the modern structure of Major League Baseball, culminating in the first World Series that same year?
Options: The American League and National League
The National League and Federal League
The Union Association and American League
The Players' League and National League
Questions.Explanation: The American League, founded in 1901, and the older National League agreed to a peace deal in 1903, launching the modern World Series era.

Questions.Prompt: What was the outcome of the very first modern World Series, played in 1903 between Boston and Pittsburgh?
Options: The series ended in a tie
Questions.Explanation: The Boston Americans (later the Red Sox) won the first World Series five games to three over the Pittsburgh Pirates.

Questions.Prompt: What is the collective name given to the added round of playoff teams, introduced in 2012, that don't win their division but still qualify for the postseason?
Questions.Explanation: The Wild Card format has expanded several times since its 1994 introduction, now including multiple teams per league.

Questions.Prompt: What year did Major League Baseball cancel its postseason entirely due to a players' strike, the only time this has happened since 1904?
Questions.Explanation: The 1994 players' strike wiped out the World Series entirely, a rare and painful chapter in the sport's labor history.

Questions.Prompt: How many teams currently make up Major League Baseball, split evenly between the American and National Leagues?
Questions.Explanation: MLB has featured 30 teams (15 per league) since the Arizona Diamondbacks and Tampa Bay Devil Rays joined in 1998.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a pitcher who specializes in coming into the game at the very end to close it out and secure the win?
Questions.Explanation: Closers are typically a team's best relief pitcher, brought in for high-leverage save situations in the final inning.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes a pitch that appears to be a strike but drops or moves out of the zone just before reaching the batter, inducing a swing and miss?
Questions.Explanation: Breaking balls like curveballs and sliders use spin to change direction late, deceiving hitters who commit to a swing.

Questions.Prompt: What unique pitch, thrown with almost no spin, is known for its unpredictable, fluttering movement that baffles both hitters and catchers?
Questions.Explanation: Knuckleball specialists like Tim Wakefield and R.A. Dickey built entire careers around the pitch's erratic, hard-to-predict flight path.

Questions.Prompt: What is a 'changeup' pitch designed to do?
Options: Look like a fastball out of the hand but arrive much slower, disrupting a batter's timing
Curve sharply downward at the last second
Rise unexpectedly through the strike zone
Questions.Explanation: A changeup relies on deceptive arm speed rather than velocity, throwing off a hitter's timing after seeing faster pitches.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a batter's turn at the plate that results in an official statistical outcome, excluding walks, sacrifices, and hit-by-pitches?
Questions.Explanation: At-bats are a subset of plate appearances used specifically to calculate batting average, excluding non-AB outcomes like walks.

Questions.Prompt: What Babe Ruth moment in the 1932 World Series became legendary, with some claiming he pointed to the outfield before hitting a home run there?
Questions.Explanation: Whether Ruth truly 'called' his home run against the Cubs remains debated, but the legend has endured for nearly a century.

Questions.Prompt: What is the traditional first pitch tradition where a dignitary, celebrity, or honored guest throws a ceremonial pitch before an MLB game begins?
Questions.Explanation: US Presidents have thrown ceremonial first pitches dating back to William Howard Taft in 1910, a tradition that continues today.

Questions.Prompt: What nickname is given to Major League Baseball's opening day, traditionally marking the unofficial start of spring?
Questions.Explanation: Opening Day carries near-holiday status among baseball fans, with the Cincinnati Reds traditionally hosting the very first game of the season.

Questions.Prompt: What warm-weather period each spring do MLB teams spend in Florida and Arizona preparing for the regular season?
Questions.Explanation: Spring training takes place across the Grapefruit League (Florida) and Cactus League (Arizona) each March.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes the informal winter leagues in countries like the Dominican Republic and Venezuela where MLB players often compete in the offseason?
Questions.Explanation: Winter ball leagues let players stay sharp and develop skills during the MLB offseason, often in front of passionate home crowds.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a rookie player's very first official MLB game appearance?
Questions.Explanation: A player's MLB debut is often a highly anticipated milestone after years working through the minor league system.

Questions.Prompt: What minor league classification sits directly below Major League Baseball, typically the last stop before a player's MLB call-up?
Questions.Explanation: Triple-A is the highest level of minor league baseball, feeding talent directly into MLB rosters.

Questions.Prompt: What is the collective term for a team's group of minor league affiliates across different classification levels?
Questions.Explanation: Teams build out their own 'farm system' of affiliated minor league clubs to develop young talent before the majors.

Questions.Prompt: What is the standard number of innings in a regulation MLB game, barring a tie requiring extra innings?
Questions.Explanation: A standard MLB game runs nine innings, with extra innings played only if the score remains tied.

Questions.Prompt: What umpire signal indicates that a runner is safe at a base?
Options: Both arms spread out horizontally, palms down
One arm raised straight up with a closed fist
Both arms crossed over the chest
One arm pointed toward the runner
Questions.Explanation: The 'safe' signal - arms spread wide, palms down - is one of the most recognizable gestures in the sport.

Questions.Prompt: What umpire signal indicates a batter or runner has been called out?
Options: A closed fist punched upward or outward
Arms spread wide with palms down
Both hands raised above the head
Questions.Explanation: The emphatic upward or outward fist punch signals an out, often delivered with dramatic flair by veteran umpires.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for the area on the field where relief pitchers warm up before entering the game?
Questions.Explanation: The bullpen, typically located down the foul lines or beyond the outfield fence, is where relievers throw practice pitches before entering.

Questions.Prompt: What piece of equipment does a batter wear to protect their hand and improve bat grip, particularly in cold or wet weather?
Questions.Explanation: Batting gloves improve grip and reduce the sting of contact, though some players famously choose to bat bare-handed.

Questions.Prompt: What is the term for a pitcher's warm-up mound located in the bullpen, separate from the game mound on the infield?
Questions.Explanation: Bullpen mounds mirror the exact height and slope of the game mound so pitchers can warm up under realistic conditions.

Questions.Prompt: What informal name is given to a batter who bats immediately after the best hitter in a lineup, protecting them from intentional walks?
Questions.Explanation: Lineup 'protection' theory suggests a dangerous hitter batting behind a star reduces the likelihood of intentional walks.

Questions.Prompt: What term is used when a batter is intentionally walked by the pitching team to avoid a dangerous confrontation, often signaled by four wide pitches or an automatic award?
Questions.Explanation: MLB simplified intentional walks in 2017, allowing managers to signal one without requiring four actual pitches to be thrown.

Questions.Prompt: What is a 'quality start,' a common modern benchmark for evaluating a starting pitcher's outing?
Options: At least six innings pitched while allowing three or fewer earned runs
Questions.Explanation: The quality start statistic became popular in the 1980s as a simple way to measure consistently solid (if not dominant) starts.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes the situation where a batter reaches base safely because of a fielder's mistake rather than a clean hit?
Questions.Explanation: Reaching 'on an error' does not count as a hit for batting average purposes, since the batter didn't earn it with a clean ball in play.

Questions.Prompt: What term describes an official scorer's ruling that credits a batter with reaching base safely due to a fielder choosing to make a play on another runner instead?
Questions.Explanation: On a fielder's choice, the defense opts to get a different runner out, letting the batter reach base without being credited a hit.
